topic: Large language model alignment using reinforcement learning from human feedback post 2022
final_review: The alignment of large language models using reinforcement learning from human feedback has gained significant attention in recent years (Köpf et al., 2023; Bai et al., 2023). This approach has been explored in various studies, including the OpenAssistant Conversations project, which aims to democratize large language model alignment (Köpf et al., 2023). Similarly, the Qwen Technical Report highlights the importance of human feedback in fine-tuning large language models (Bai et al., 2023). The use of transfer learning, as surveyed by Weiss and Khoshgoftaar (2016), has also been applied to large language models, enabling them to adapt to new tasks and domains. The application of artificial intelligence in higher education has been reviewed by Zawacki‐Richter and Marín (2019), who emphasize the need for educators to be involved in the development and implementation of AI-powered systems. In the context of large language models, this highlights the importance of human oversight and feedback in ensuring that these models are aligned with human values and goals (Dwivedi et al., 2023). The use of deep learning techniques, as overviewed by Sarker (2021) and Alzubaidi and Zhang (2021), has been instrumental in the development of large language models. However, the interpretability of these models remains a challenge, with studies such as those by Hassija and Chamola (2023) and Ali and Abuhmed (2023) highlighting the need for explainable artificial intelligence. The GPT-4 Technical Report (Wijegunarathna et al., 2023) and the Survey of Large Language Models (Zhao et al., 2023) provide an overview of the current state of large language models and their potential applications. However, the alignment of these models with human values and goals remains an open challenge, with studies such as those by Järvelä and Zhao (2025) highlighting the need for hybrid intelligence approaches that combine human and artificial intelligence. In conclusion, the alignment of large language models using reinforcement learning from human feedback is an active area of research, with various studies exploring its applications and challenges (Köpf et al., 2023; Bai et al., 2023; Dwivedi et al., 2023). Further research is needed to address the gaps and contradictions in the current literature, including the need for more transparent and explainable models (Hassija et al., 2023; Ali et al., 2023). The proceedings of the 28th International Conference on Computational Linguistics (Zhu et al., 2020) and the taxonomy of metaverse applications (Park et al., 2022) also highlight the potential of large language models in various domains.
